liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): Reviewer recalls the band playing hot and Jerry on fire; the crowd seemed stunned afterward; Jerry flailed at the end and skipped the final refrain, leaving the band confused until Phil started Box of Rain [16][21]
- **Box of Rain** (2 reviews): With nobody sure what came next after Dew, Phil launched into Box of Rain; After the energy building through Morning Dew, Box of Rain relaxed the crowd and the room felt cooler [16][22]
- **Help is on the Way** (1 review): The Help>Slipknot>Franklin's sequence is called pretty strong, and Eyes is strong too [21]
- **Saint of Circumstance** (1 review): Saint sounded a bit rocky because the band was still working it back into the repertoire [21]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): This soundboard has a rather harsh edit near the end of Eyes [14]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The young first-timer was especially thrilled to hear The Other One and Box of Rain [25]

## Setlist highlights

- **Valley Road**: rare: 7 archived performances [26]

## The recordings

- **gd90-12-13.sbd.unknown.4988.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 156 min; rated 4.5/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: Rated A+ for sound, but with occasional digital pops and static in places; Sounds good but is heavily glitched, especially during Eyes; reviewer suggests the other soundboard for a coherent version [14][20]
- **gd1990-12-13.149746.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 158 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd1990-12-13.140290.MTX.PhotoLeon.t-flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 163 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [5]. Said about its sound: Levels swing like a roller coaster through Jack Straw, Sugaree and Wang Dang Doodle before settling; Second-set levels are uncertain and were normalized to -1.2dB [5]
- **gd90-12-13.sbd-matrix.vernon.24411.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 158 min; rated 3.43/5 by 7 [6]. Said about its sound: Matrix recording's sound quality is described as decent, not bad [17]

## Around the show

- Reviewer, at the second of three shows, had a mail-order floor ticket for Sec AAA, Row 1, seat 11 [19]
- Many women spun in the hallways during Jerry songs, dresses flowing, while some sat during Bobby songs [22]
- It was cold outside with strong wind blowing [22]
- Reviewer's first Dead show: attended at age 11 with their dad on a school night [25]
- Reviewer ranks it their favorite of the three-night run, apart from the Dark Stars at the other shows [15]
- Reviewer likes the whole 1990 McNichols run and calls this one of the few 90s shows they enjoy [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd90-12-13.sbd.unknown.4988.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard to DAT to CDR, extracted with EAC and encoded to SHN; ripped by John Zei [1]
- **gd1990-12-13.149746.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  April 16, 2020; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [4]. Also: File set is 16 bit at 44.1 kHz [4]
- **gd1990-12-13.140290.MTX.PhotoLeon.t-flac1648**: transferred by Matrix by photoleon; source: flac16/48kHz ; Two Source Matrix: Source #1 (shnid: 108981) Recording Info: SBD -> Dat (48k) and Rick Katzeff recording: Schoeps CMC521 configured in a 90… [5]. Also: Source DAT is labeled spaced array; Katzeff adjusted levels in the first three first-set songs [5]
- **gd90-12-13.sbd-matrix.vernon.24411.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard Matrix:D-> DAT [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1990-12-13 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1990-12-13-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [27]
